outcome.technical: DESIGN. _worktrees.py gains the move: advance_plan (pure: work = changed paths outside the caller's records, overlap = work that moved, a non-empty overlap is the refusal naming every overlapping path), advance_tree (refuses before any write unless the tree's HEAD IS the base, git describes the span and the tree, and no work path moved; takes a copy of every changed path in memory and on disk under the tree's own admin dir (audit-advance/), puts record paths back at the base one path at a time, runs `git checkout -q --detach <head>` WITHOUT -f, then compares every work path byte for byte; any failure undoes from the copy (`checkout -f --detach <base>` + bytes written back + re-verified), restored True and the copy removed, or restored False with the copy kept and named), advance_task_tree (reads the base from THIS task's marker, moves, rewrites the marker: base = new head, baseMoves += {from, to, moved, at}; a move whose marker could not be written is advanced WITH error, the one state where tree and record disagree), and write_record (the marker writer, moved down from manage-worktrees so the mover records through the one writer). No rebase, no commit, no rewritten SHA anywhere: drive-phase.py's rule 'never rebase - it rewrites the task commit SHAs' stays true. drive-phase.py: gate_step calls advance_member before refresh_member_records for a member tree; advance_member compares the wave's recorded base with git_head, and when the head moved calls _worktrees.advance_task_tree in-process (records = the wave's refreshed record paths via _invariants.is_record_path); on success updates wave.bases, writes a `task.tree.advanced` journal row (parent = old base, commit = new base, changes = the files that moved) and a did-line; a refused move leaves the tree and gates it where it is, as before, saying the overlap on the did-line; a move that could not be put back or whose marker could not record it stops the drive. Every gate a member gets - first gate of a returned task, a rerun, a retry - goes through gate_step, so all three follow the head. The run's record: the gate row's testedState.head is the new head (ab1), the journal row (ab2), wave.bases and the marker's baseMoves (tv1); integrate-task.py reads the base from the marker, so the integration diffs the work against the new base (ab3 closes with only the member's bytes; tv2: task-add adoption hands back the new base); a carry made after the move is a commit on the tree's HEAD, i.e. the new base. The stamp's scopeDigest is not among the fields a stale grade names after a move (observed did-line `stamp stale (moved head; content)` in the ab-block run - head moves by design). manage-worktrees.py: _write_record delegates to _worktrees.write_record (same file, same bytes: json indent=1 sort_keys + newline, newline='\n'); no verb was added, because a verb needs a PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md code span (lint e1) and a new import edge changes the guide's module-map fence (lint g1), both outside this task's files - an earlier draft had a `task-advance` verb, measured red on exactly those two lints, and was taken out. TESTS. tests/test__worktrees.py: _advance_cases av1-av12 against a REAL repository (base holds a.txt, b.txt, d.txt, docs/r.json; head moves b.txt and docs/r.json; work edits a.txt, adds untracked n.txt, deletes d.txt). tests/test_drive_phase.py: new stage ab-block (_wave_advance_cases ab1, ab2, ab3, ab1m RED TWIN, ab4); two existing cases adjusted for the new, intended behaviour: wq2 now compares the member tree's files minus those the phase moved between the tree's old base and its new head (the tree now legitimately moves past P1.1's integrated src/f1.txt; the case still asserts src/f2.txt is not among them and is byte-identical), and the wq1m twin also disables advance_member, since bringing the tree to the head brings the committed records too. tests/test_manage_worktrees.py: _advance_cases tv1-tv4 over trees task-add made and marked. MUTATION TABLE (probe in a scratch copy, anchors asserted to land exactly once, __pycache__ purged each cycle; probe at <scratchpad>/probe/mutations.py, output probe2.log beside it): overlap never computed -> av3 av5 tv3 red (av4 and ab4 stay green: git's non-forced checkout refuses the same overlap and names the file - two independent guards); byte check skipped -> av7; checkout forced -> av1; records counted as work -> av6 av12; undo writes nothing back -> av7; HEAD-is-base check dropped -> av11; already-at-head check dropped -> av10; marker not rewritten -> tv1 tv2 ab3; drive never moves the tree -> ab1 ab2 ab3; no journal row -> ab2; forced checkout + no byte check -> av2; overlap ignored + forced checkout -> av4; copy kept after a clean undo -> av8; refused checkout read as a move -> av9; another task's marker read -> tv4; refused move not said -> ab4. ab1m is itself the red twin of ab1 (the driver with advance_member disabled records a red at the old base).
